result.title: Cross-Domain Joint-Embedding Pretraining For Heterogeneous Industrial Time Series
result.comment: Submitted to International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP) on Sept. 24, 2026
result.summary: Industrial predictive maintenance and manufacturing tasks frequently contain abundant sensor measurements, but with limited labeled data. We investigate cross-domain self-supervised pretraining using joint-embedding predictive architecture for heterogeneous industrial time series (JEPA-HITS), which learns one encoder from various domains such as battery, semiconductor chemical mechanical planarization (CMP), computer numerical control (CNC) machining, and bearing while preserving dataset-specific temporal scales. We evaluate representation reuse on regression and classification problems under reduced-label downstream training, and leave-one-domain-out (LODO) pretraining. Compared with the same architecture initialized randomly, LODO pretraining reduces RMSE from 10.72 to 7.95 on battery remaining useful life (RUL), 4.34 to 3.89 on CMP, and 13.53 to 11.72 on tool wear regression, while improving bearing fault diagnosis macro-F1 from 0.547 to 0.737. Overall results suggest that unlabeled time series measurements from heterogeneous industrial processes can provide reusable representations for downstream learning with limited labeled data.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 JEPA-HITS，用联合嵌入预测架构在电池、CMP、CNC、轴承等异构工业时间序列上做跨域自监督预训练，共享一个编码器同时保留各数据集的时间尺度，并在少标注下游回归与分类任务及留一域预训练设置下评估表示复用效果。
